markdown_content: # Everywear To Snap AR Tutorial (English/한국어) This document details the process of converting garments created in Clo or Marvelous Designer into Snapchat AR filters using Everywhere and Lens Studio. It covers garment preparation, optimization, rigging, texture baking, and Lens Studio integration, including technical requirements and publishing steps. --- ## Introduction and Overview This section introduces the concept of creating custom AR garment filters for Snapchat using Everywhere, Clo, and Marvelous Designer. It highlights the tools and workflow for transforming garments into Snapchat-compatible AR lenses. - **Snapchat**: Social network focused on photo/video sharing. - **Everywhere**: Tool for garment optimization and texture baking. - **Clo / Marvelous Designer**: 3D garment design software. - **Lens Studio**: Software for creating and publishing Snapchat AR filters. Before starting, users should complete the basic Everywhere tutorial for foundational knowledge. --- ## Lens Studio Requirements and Setup This section outlines the technical specifications required by Lens Studio to ensure AR filters work correctly on Snapchat. - Use **Lens Studio version 4.49** or later. - Mesh triangle count: **Under 100,000 triangles**, ideally below **60,000 polygons**. - Texture size: **Max 2048 x 2048 pixels**; tutorial uses **1024 x 1024**. - Lens file size: **Under 8 MB**. - Download the **body mesh for Lens Studio** (FBX with skeleton) from provided resources; required for garment rigging. Refer to Lens Studio documentation for detailed guidelines and manual. --- ## Preparing Garments in Clo / Marvelous Designer This section describes importing, fitting, optimizing, rigging, and baking textures for garments in Clo or Marvelous Designer using Everywhere. ### Importing and Fitting - Download garment files from **Kinect** marketplace. - Import the Lens Studio body mesh (FBX with skeleton) into Clo or Marvelous Designer. - Import the garment file into Clo/Marvelous Designer. - Fit garment on the imported avatar. - If avatar mesh is low-poly with angular surfaces, use: - Clo: Property Editor → Surface → Divide Mesh to smooth. - Marvelous Designer: Property Editor → Smooth Avatar. ### Garment Optimization and Rigging - Open Everywhere plugin inside Clo/Marvelous Designer. - Set garment optimization target to **60,000 triangles**. - Run garment optimization and simulate again. - Click **Apply** under rigging for auto-rigging. - Optionally create skin weight adjustments or sculpt brushes for shape refinement. - Exit brush window when done. ### Texture Baking - Set image (texture) size before UV packing (e.g., 1024 x 1024). - Pack UVs with seam size configured. - Bake texture maps: generate normal maps, ambient occlusion, etc. - Materials will be automatically created per UV tile. - For simplicity, use one material or divide materials as needed. ### Exporting for Lens Studio - Click **Upload** in Everywhere. - Uncheck avatar export if only garment is needed. - Select required texture maps. - Upload to Everywhere Connect. - Download the exported FBX and texture maps (usually as a ZIP containing .fbx and texture files). --- ## Importing and Setting Up in Lens Studio This section explains how to assemble the garment and body mesh within Lens Studio to prepare the AR lens. ### Rigging and Mesh Setup - Open Lens Studio, create a new project. - Add **Full Body Mesh** object. - Rename the body mesh object to match the garment name. - Import the garment FBX file (from Everywhere Connect) into Resources. - In the body mesh inspector: - Set **External Mesh Pose** to **A Pose** or **T Pose** depending on garment creation. - Assign the imported garment FBX as the external mesh. - Set **Body Index** to 0. - Verify garment appears correctly in preview. ### Material Setup - Import texture maps into Resources. - Select garment mesh object; open material settings. - Make material **Two-Sided** to render both sides of the garment. - Add a **Uber PBR** material (Physically Based Rendering). - Assign texture maps (normal, albedo, ambient occlusion, etc.) to the Uber PBR material. - Apply the Uber PBR material to the garment mesh. ### Adding Body Occluder - Add another **Full Body Mesh** object as a **body occluder** to cover hidden areas under the garment. - Parent the occluder mesh to the garment’s 3D body tracking zero. - Delete any redundant body tracking objects. - Set occluder mesh pose to **A Pose** and body index to 0. - Position the occluder at transform position X = 0. - Apply a transparent occluder material: - Add **Occluder** material from Lens Studio materials. - Assign occluder material to the occluder mesh. - Confirm occlusion works correctly in the preview window. --- ## Previewing and Publishing the Lens This section covers final steps to test, validate, and publish the AR garment filter on Snapchat. ### Previewing - Link your Snapchat account in Lens Studio. - Use **Send to Snapchat** button to preview the lens on your device. - Verify garment fits and animates correctly. ### Publishing - Check lens file size via Performance panel; ensure it is under 8 MB. - Fill in project info: lens name, description, category, tags. - Upload or record a preview video. - Set a thumbnail image of the garment (captured or rendered). - Click **Publish Lens**. - In Snapchat’s My Lens page: - Select folder for the lens. - Submit lens for review. - Lens will show status as **Processing** and update to **Available** once approved. - After approval, click **Publish** to finalize. - Optionally adjust visibility and sharing settings. - Download Snapcode or link to share the lens. - Use Snapchat app to scan the Snapcode and try the custom filter. --- # Summary This tutorial provides a comprehensive workflow from garment creation in Clo or Marvelous Designer to deploying a custom AR garment filter on Snapchat via Everywhere and Lens Studio. Key technical requirements, optimization, rigging, texture baking, and Lens Studio configuration steps are detailed to enable creators to build performant and visually accurate AR garment lenses.
